subject.title: fix(codex): require explicit final source delivery

question: Should Codex message-tool-only completion use a mandatory explicit `final` contract, or should OpenClaw keep the existing terminal contract and rely on the narrower prompt-only fix?
rationale: Making `final` mandatory is structurally robust but changes the Codex model-facing tool contract; preserving omitted-marker compatibility leaves the reported failure possible, and the open alternatives embody different permanent policies.

options.title: Require explicit final
options.body: Make the Codex-only schema require `final`, keep progress non-terminal, define absent-marker failure behavior, and require exact-head live proof.

options.title: Use prompt-only steering
options.body: Prefer the proof-positive narrower approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100156 and close the competing runtime-contract branches after selection.

options.title: Keep optional compatibility
options.body: Retain absent-marker terminal behavior and explicitly accept that prompt noncompliance can reproduce the early-release bug.

recommendation.title: Require explicit final
recommendation.body: Make the Codex-only schema require `final`, keep progress non-terminal, define absent-marker failure behavior, and require exact-head live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the current terminal source-reply classifier and provides the strongest available history signal for selecting its successor contract.
